prompt: In scaled dot-product attention, what do Q, K, and V represent?
choices: Three independent random initializations averaged together for stability
Learned linear projections of the input: what a token is looking for (Q), what it contains (K), and what it offers if attended to (V)
The three transformer layers stacked in sequence
Query = input embedding, Key = position embedding, Value = the output logits

prompt: Why does scaled dot-product attention divide by √d_k specifically (not d_k, not a constant)?
choices: It's an arbitrary hyperparameter tuned per model with no principled justification

Because the variance of a dot product between two random d_k-dimensional unit-variance vectors is d_k, so dividing by √d_k renormalizes the standard deviation back to ~1 regardless of dimension, keeping softmax out of its low-gradient saturated regime
To make the attention weights sum to d_k instead of 1
Because PyTorch's softmax implementation requires inputs scaled below 1.0

prompt: What does multi-head attention add on top of single-head attention?
choices: A larger d_model, nothing structurally different

It lets the model jointly attend to information from several different representation subspaces in parallel, since a single softmax distribution per token can't represent multiple distinct relationships at once
A second, independent softmax normalization for numerical stability
It replaces the dot-product similarity with cosine similarity

prompt: Why does a transformer need an explicit positional encoding, when an RNN does not?
choices: Transformers use too much memory to track position implicitly
Self-attention computes the same output for any permutation of the input tokens — it has no inherent notion of order, unlike an RNN whose recurrence processes tokens in sequence
Positional encoding is only needed for decoder-only models, not encoders
RNNs also require positional encoding; it's a modern addition unrelated to recurrence

prompt: Which architecture is BERT, and how does its self-attention differ from GPT's?
choices: BERT is decoder-only with causal masking, same as GPT

BERT is encoder-only with unmasked (bidirectional) self-attention, so every token can attend to every other token including future ones; GPT is decoder-only with causal masking restricting each token to only past tokens
BERT and GPT are both encoder-decoder models with cross-attention
BERT has no self-attention at all, only convolutions

prompt: According to the original paper's complexity comparison, what is the key structural advantage of a self-attention layer over a recurrent layer, despite self-attention having worse (quadratic in n) per-layer complexity when sequence length n exceeds dimension d?
choices: Self-attention requires no learned parameters at all
Self-attention has a maximum path length of O(1) between any two positions (fully parallel, direct connection), versus O(n) for a recurrent layer, and O(1) sequential operations versus O(n)

Self-attention layers cannot be stacked, so there is only ever one layer to account for
